messages:
Ada: Heads-up — noticed a regression in small-batch tail latency after the v2.2.1 heuristic change. Nsight timeline shows host->device memcpy 'sandwiching' compute kernels with a ~6–12ms CPU scheduling gap right before our KV cache prefetch. My hunch: kernel-selection now picks a larger conv kernel that increases overlap with cudaMemcpy streams and ends up blocking async copies.

Jordan: Can you upload the qdrep/trace? which commit range to bisect? Also: is this on Dedicated infra or local repro?

Ada: Link: https://internal-traces/repro/2771234567.qdrep (short-lived link). Repro on dedicated-capi-staging (A100). Suspect commits between 45..52 (batcher/heuristics).

Sam: Pasted the nsys command I used to generate that trace:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas,osrt,osrt_sync -o out.qdrep 
PYTHONPATH=. python -m perf.repro --batch-size 2 --seq-len 512
```
The timeline snapshot: hostMemcpyAsync (stream 2) -> small kernel (stream 1) -> big conv (stream 1) -> hostMemcpyAsync (stream 2). The 1st memcpy appears to wake kernel but then CPU has a gap before prefetch thread runs.

Lee: Quick thought — if the conv kernel chosen has different stream affinity (we changed kernel-launch flags to prefer stream-1 ordering under the heuristic), we can accidentally serialize the copy+kernel across streams. Also saw a bunch of `sched_switch` entries in perfetto around the same time (CPU preempting the prefetch thread). That explains the 6–12ms window.

perf-bot: Automated summary: top time slices in trace: [cuMemcpyAsync: 44%], [customConvKernel_v3: 33%], [KV-prefetch-thread wake: 6%]. Hotspots: kernel launch latency spiked x1.8 vs baseline. Candidate regression: batcher changes that bump seq grouping from 4->8.

Ada: Repro plan: 1) try forcing legacy kernel via KERNEL_FORCE=legacy_conv to see if overlap improves; 2) bisect commits 45..52 with a perf microtest focused on 1-2 token latency; 3) run nsys with thread scheduling markers (osrt) and perfetto to confirm cpu preemption. Assign Jordan + Lee.

Jordan: I'll add a perf microtest in the CI job and run the bisect locally on staging. Will post new qdrep by EOD. @Lee can you try KERNEL_FORCE run and check stream priorities?

Lee: On it. Quick local check shows forcing legacy_conv reduces measured tail by ~8%. CPU prefetch still has occasional 5ms wake delay, so two orthogonal issues: kernel selection and occasional scheduler gap.

Sam: Putting the short timeline ascii here for quick eyeballing:

[time  ms]  stream1: |---kernel_small---|---kernel_big----|
           stream2: |--memcpy--|                     |--memcpy--|
           CPU:     |----prefetch thread (blocked by sched gap)----|

Ada: Good catch. If kernel change is the bigger impact, we can revert kernel-selection heuristic and land a separate fix for the prefetch thread priority (increase niceness -> real-time hint).

Jordan: Action items: (1) bisect commits 45..52 (Jordan), (2) KERNEL_FORCE experiment (Lee), (3) add perfetto/osrt markers to repro and re-run trace (Sam), (4) if repro confirms, open rollback PR for heuristic (Ada). I'll update this thread with the new traces. :thumbsup:

Sam: Will attach the new qdrep link once the run finishes.

Ada: Thanks — please ping here with the new trace. If we confirm cpu preemption is significant, I'll file a perf-regression ticket and tag eng-sre for kernel scheduler tuning.
